Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

compare verb

also compare with, compared with, comparison, liken

classical

Cic. Off. 1.11 (Lewis & Short): similitūdinēs comparat
Traupman 294: comparāre cum

comparō, comparāre, comparāvī, comparātum

verb, first conjugation; with cum and the ablative, or the dative

From compār, “matched”: not the same word as comparō, “get ready”, which Lewis & Short gives as a separate entry. A comparison is comparātiō (Traupman 294).

Other words

  • cōnferō, cōnferre, contulī, collātum — compare, set side by side

    verb, irregular (like ferō); with cum and the ablative, or the dative · also used · classical · Phaedr. 4.25.3: cōnferre nostrīs tū potes tē laudibus?

  • compōnō, compōnere, composuī, compositum — compare (small things with great)

    verb, third conjugation; with an accusative and a dative · also used · classical · Verg. G. 4.176: sī parva licet compōnere magnīs; Verg. E. 1.23: sīc parvīs compōnere magna solēbam

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Acc., Verg., Ov.)

  • comparātiō, comparātiōnis f. — comparison

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 294

Examples

  • sī parva licet compōnere magnīs

    if one may compare small things with greatVerg. G. 4.176

  • formīca et musca contendēbant ācriter quae plūris esset. musca sīc coepit prior: cōnferre nostrīs tū potes tē laudibus?

    The ant and the fly were arguing hotly which was worth more. The fly began: “Can you compare yourself with my merits?”Phaedr. 4.25.1–3

  • Hunc pānem cum illō cōnfer: uter tibi magis placet?

    Compare this bread with that one: which do you like better?composed

See also same, different, value.
